title: Add structured logging conventions and typed application exceptions
description:
Create the observability logging foundation and the typed application exception hierarchy using only the Python standard library.

mike_trade/observability/logging.py: implement a JSON log formatter (`JsonFormatter`) that emits one JSON object per line with at least: timestamp as ISO-8601 UTC with an explicit offset, level, logger, message, and any structured `extra` context fields (for example mode, account_id, scenario, symbol, strategy, order_id, correlation_id). Provide `configure_logging(level: str = 'INFO', *, json_output: bool = True, stream=None) -> None`, which is idempotent (calling it twice must not duplicate handlers), and `get_logger(name: str) -> logging.Logger`. Implement secret redaction: any field whose key matches a sensitive pattern (api_key, secret, token, password, authorization, APCA-API-KEY-ID, APCA-API-SECRET-KEY, case-insensitive) is replaced with '***REDACTED***' before serialization. Decimal and datetime values must serialize deterministically (Decimal as a string, datetime as ISO-8601 UTC). No file handlers or network sinks in this task.

mike_trade/domain/errors.py: define a broker-neutral exception hierarchy rooted at `MikeTradeError`, carrying an optional machine-readable `code` and a `context` mapping. Include at minimum: ConfigurationError, LiveTradingNotAuthorizedError, ModeIsolationError, StaleMarketDataError, ReconciliationDriftError, InsufficientBuyingPowerError, EntryBlockedError, UnsupportedOrderCapabilityError, BrokerError (with BrokerRejectedError and BrokerUnavailableError subclasses), PersistenceError, and StrategyError. This module must not import any adapter, broker SDK, or third-party package.

Before editing, inspect:
- pyproject.toml (read-only) for ruff/mypy settings if present
- mike_trade/ package layout (read-only)
- PLAN_SKELETON.json purpose (read-only) for the fail-closed, mode-isolation, and reconciliation error categories
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/observability/logging.py defines JsonFormatter, configure_logging, and get_logger using only the standard library
Each log record is a single valid JSON line containing timestamp (UTC with offset), level, logger, and message keys
Structured extra fields appear as top-level JSON keys; Decimal values serialize as strings and datetimes as ISO-8601 UTC
Fields whose keys match api_key/secret/token/password/authorization (case-insensitive) are emitted as '***REDACTED***'
Calling configure_logging twice leaves exactly one handler attached by this module on the root/application logger
mike_trade/domain/errors.py defines MikeTradeError and every listed subclass; each subclass is an instance of MikeTradeError
MikeTradeError accepts and exposes optional code and context attributes
mike_trade/domain/errors.py imports nothing from mike_trade.brokers, alpaca, or any third-party package
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
add third-party logging dependencies or edit pyproject.toml
import broker SDKs or adapters from domain/errors.py
run broad test suites, backtests, or create broker orders
